definitions.gloss: leg (of a person or animal); limb
definitions.explanation: The whole limb from the hip to the foot — what supports the body and is used for walking. Distinct from {足|あし} (foot), though the readings are identical and the words overlap in casual writing.
The supporting parts under a table, chair, camera tripod, or similar object.

examples.japanese: ⟦{長時間|ちょうじかん}→長時間：10165_choujikan⟧⟦{座|すわ}っていた→座る：00757_suwaru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で{脚|あし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧しびれてしまった。
examples.english: Because I was sitting for a long time, my legs went numb.

examples.japanese: ⟦テーブル→テーブル：04488_teeburu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{脚|あし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ぐらつく。
⟦{椅子|いす}→椅子：00706_isu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{脚|あし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{一本|いっぽん}→一本：08888_ippon⟧⟦{折|お}れた→折れる：01266_oreru⟧。
examples.english: One of the chair's legs broke.

examples.japanese: ⟦カメラ→カメラ：04417_kamera⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{三脚|さんきゃく}→三脚：06993_sankyaku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{脚|あし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{広|ひろ}げて→広げる：01981_hirogeru⟧⟦{安定|あんてい}→安定：01703_antei⟧⟦させる→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Spread the legs of the camera tripod to stabilize it.

notes:
{脚|あし} and ⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧ share the same reading but differ in scope:
- {脚|あし}: the whole leg (hip to foot), plus furniture/equipment legs
- ⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧: the foot proper (ankle down), and by extension the lower limb in casual use

In everyday writing, ⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧ is often used for both. {脚|あし} is preferred when the context emphasizes the leg as a limb (anatomy, fashion, sports) or when referring to non-human "legs."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {脚|あし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{長|なが}い→長い：00491_nagai⟧: to have long legs
- {脚|あし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{組|く}む→組む：02050_kumu⟧: to cross one's legs
- ⟦テーブル→テーブル：04488_teeburu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{脚|あし}: the legs of a table
- {脚|あし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{細|ほそ}い→細い：02962_hosoi⟧: to have thin legs

COMPOUNDS:
- ⟦{三脚|さんきゃく}→三脚：06993_sankyaku⟧: tripod
- ⟦{脚立|きゃたつ}→脚立：06315_kyatatsu⟧: stepladder
- ⟦{脚本|きゃくほん}→脚本：04459_kyakuhon⟧: script, screenplay
